english: An ordered triple $(x,y,z)$ is chosen at random from the set of all ordered triples of non-negative integers satisfying $x+y+z=23$, all such triples being equally likely. Let $p$ be the probability that each of $x$, $y$, $z$ is at most $11$, and let $q$ be the probability that each of $x$, $y$, $z$ is at least $1$. Then the value of $p-q$ is ______.
hindi: समीकरण $x+y+z=23$ को सन्तुष्ट करने वाले अऋणात्मक पूर्णांकों के सभी क्रमित त्रिकों के समुच्चय से एक क्रमित त्रिक $(x,y,z)$ यादृच्छया चुना जाता है, ऐसे सभी त्रिक समसम्भाव्य हैं। माना कि $p$ इसकी प्रायिकता है कि $x$, $y$, $z$ में से प्रत्येक अधिकतम $11$ है, तथा $q$ इसकी प्रायिकता है कि $x$, $y$, $z$ में से प्रत्येक कम से कम $1$ है। तब $p-q$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $p$: triples with $x\ge12$: $x''+y+z=11$, $\binom{13}{2}=78$; two of them $\ge12$ is impossible ($24>23$); so $300-3\cdot78=66$, $p=\dfrac{66}{300}=0.22$
solution_full: Sample space: the number of non-negative integer solutions of $x+y+z=23$ is $\binom{23+3-1}{3-1}=\binom{25}{2}=300$; all are equally likely.
Lower bounds ($q$): with $x=x'+1$, $y=y'+1$, $z=z'+1$ and $x',y',z'\ge0$, the equation becomes $x'+y'+z'=20$, which has $\binom{22}{2}=231$ solutions. So $q=\dfrac{231}{300}=0.77$.

Upper bounds ($p$): let $A_{x}$ be the solutions with $x\ge12$. Putting $x=x''+12$ gives $x''+y+z=11$: $\binom{13}{2}=78$ solutions. The same holds for $A_{y}$, $A_{z}$. Two variables cannot both be at least $12$ because their sum would exceed $23$, so the sets are disjoint.
Hence the number with every variable at most $11$ is $300-3\cdot78=66$ and $p=\dfrac{66}{300}=0.22$.
originality_note: New: one uniform model on the solutions of x + y + z = 23 scored by an upper-bound event and a lower-bound event, so the beggar's method is used three ways (total, shifted lower bound, excess over an upper bound) (way 5). Closest known: 'number of solutions of x + y + z = n with each variable at most k'. Different because: the uniform-solution probability model and the comparison of the two bounded counts are the question.

concept_use.Probability computed using permutations: p and q are favourable solutions divided by the 300 equally likely solutions.
concept_use.Non-negative integral solutions of x1+x2: The total C(25,2) = 300 and the shifted counts C(22,2) and C(13,2) are beggar's-method counts.
concept_use.Integral solutions with lower and upper: The upper bound x, y, z <= 11 is handled by removing the solutions with a variable >= 12, and the lower bound by the shift x = x' + 1.
